description: Equipo para el desafío de focos de calor MODIS/VIIRS. Vamos a construir una app web con el calendario histórico del fuego para cualquier zona, empezando por Catamarca: cuántos focos hubo cada mes desde 2003 y si el mes actual es inusual. Coordina un licenciado en Estadística. Buscamos gente de programación (Python o web), SIG o teledetección, ciencias ambientales o manejo del fuego, y diseño o comunicación. No hace falta experiencia en temas espaciales: sí ganas de trabajar con datos reales.
summary: Calendario del Fuego (Fire Calendar) is a free, bilingual web app that turns 24 years of NASA FIRMS hot spots into one consistent record of fire activity for Argentina, by province and department. Since 2012, fires have been detected by MODIS (1 km pixels) and by the more sensitive VIIRS (375 m). Simply adding up all satellites makes fire look +305 % higher than in 2003–2011; measured on one scale, it is actually 35 % lower. We harmonize the record by converting VIIRS into MODIS-equivalent values with a ratio for each province, season and day/night overpass. The ratios are calibrated on 2012–2022 and stabilized with empirical-Bayes shrinkage. Every month comes with a 90 % uncertainty interval. Tested on held-out years, total error was −1.6 %. The app shows fire calendars, maps of exact hot spots, comparisons with officially reported burned area, and links with rainfall, humidity and temperature.
details:
Calendario del Fuego (Fire Calendar) turns 24 years of NASA satellite hot spots into one consistent record of fire activity for Argentina. You can explore it by province and department in a free bilingual web app: https://calendariodelfuego.streamlit.app/

The problem. Since 2012, fire has been detected by two satellite systems: MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21). VIIRS pixels are 375 m wide, while MODIS pixels are 1 km, so VIIRS sees much smaller fires. Simply adding up the detections of all five satellites makes fire look +305 % higher since 2012 than in 2003–2011. Once both systems are measured on a single scale, the level is actually 35 % lower. Without harmonization, any trend built from FIRMS data is an artifact of the sensors, not of the fires.

How it works.

1. Cleaning. We clean 6 million FIRMS detections. We keep vegetation fires above a confidence threshold and remove persistent static heat sources (974 cells).

2. A common unit. We count both sensors in the same unit, the 0.01° cell-day, separately for day and night overpasses.

3. Conversion. We convert VIIRS to MODIS-equivalent values with a ratio estimated for each of 192 strata (province × season × day/night). The ratios are calibrated on 2012–2022, when Aqua and Suomi NPP flew in the same orbit. Empirical-Bayes shrinkage (province → region → country) keeps estimates stable where fires are rare. NOAA-20 is first scaled to Suomi NPP, so the record continues after Suomi NPP stopped delivering data in November 2026.

4. Uncertainty. We propagate uncertainty with 1,000 simulations (negative binomial counts). Every month therefore carries a 90 % interval and a probability of being unusual.

5. Validation. We compared four models on held-out years (fit 2012–2018, test 2019–2022), with the selection rule written before the test. The chosen model's total error is −1.6 %, and its 90 % interval covered 86.5 % of the held-out province-months.

What the app shows.

- A month-by-year fire calendar, with counts or "compared with normal".

- Yearly and average monthly patterns.

- The current period vs the same days in past years.

- Exact hot spot locations on a map, by satellite.

- Department-level comparisons.

- Satellite detections next to the burned area officially reported to Argentina's Ministry of Environment.

- Fire activity against rainfall, humidity and temperature.

Benefits and intended impact. Fire brigades, provincial environment agencies, researchers and journalists get a trend they can trust, one they can't get today by downloading FIRMS data. The app answers practical questions:

- Is this fire season unusual for this province?

- When does the fire season peak?

- Where are fires concentrated?

- Do dry seasons predict worse fire years?

That supports planning of prevention and resources. Because the method only needs FIRMS data and administrative boundaries, it can be replicated in any country.

Tools.

- Code: Python (pandas, NumPy, DuckDB, Parquet) for the data pipeline, and R (glmmTMB) for the alternative mixed model.

- App: Streamlit and Plotly.

- Hosting and code: GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud.

- Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m), Argentina's official burned-area statistics, administrative boundaries, and monthly climate data [fuente].

- Hardware: a personal laptop.

Creativity. Instead of mixing sensors or discarding one, the project translates VIIRS into MODIS-equivalent values and is honest about the error: every number comes with its uncertainty. The calendar view also turns a statistical correction into something anyone can read at a glance.

Factors considered.

- Different pixel sizes and detection sensitivity.

- Aqua's orbital drift after 2022.

- The end of Suomi NPP data.

- Day vs night differences.

- Small provinces with few fires.

- False detections from industrial heat sources.

- The difference between "heat seen from space" and "hectares counted on the ground" (never plotted on one axis).

- Accessibility: Spanish and English, mobile-friendly, plain-language explanations in every view.
